data.name: Vasudha
data.long_meaning: Vasudha is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'vasud' which means 'abode'. According to Hindu mythology, it is believed that Vasudha is the abode of all living beings. This name is also associated with the goddess of the same name, who is known to be the mother of all creatures.

vedic_reference.note: Vasudha is mentioned in the Rigveda (10.116.4) as a goddess associated with water and the earth. She is also considered to be the personification of the earth's bountiful gifts, such as water, food, and other resources.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vasudha holds a deep cultural significance for Hindus. It is believed that the name encapsulates the essence of unconditional love, compassion, and duty towards all living beings. It reflects the Hindu belief in the unity and interconnectedness of all life forms.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Vasudha represents the ultimate goal of self-realization and enlightenment. It reminds us of our inherent connection to the universe and encourages us to cultivate a deeply compassionate and selfless attitude towards all beings. It is said that those named Vasudha are blessed with a deep sense of inner peace and the ability to foster harmony in their relationships and communities.

historical_references.reference: Vasudha was the name of the goddess of the earth in ancient Hindu mythology. She was often depicted as the wife of Vishnu and the mother of Prithvi, the god of the earth.
historical_references.time_period: Vedic and Epics period (circa 1500 BCE – 500 CE)

historical_references.reference: Vasudha was also the name of a legendary queen in ancient India, known for her exceptional beauty and wisdom. She ruled over the Vale of Kashmir and was revered as a goddess by her people.
